questions.knowledge_point: Finding Points That Satisfy the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals
questions.problem: Find all values of $c$ that satisfy the mean value theorem for integrals for  $f(x)=6{x}^{2}$ on the interval $[-1,2].$
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the mean value theorem for integrals, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c)(b-a) & ={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ f(c) & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2-(-1)}{\int }_{-1}^{2}6{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{3}\cdot (2{x}^{3})|}_{-1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[2(2)^{3}-2(-1)^{3}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot 18 \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the expression for $f(x)$ to solve for the value of $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c) & =6 \\ 6{c}^{2} & =6 \\ {c}^{2} & =1 \\ c & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find all values of $c$ that satisfy the mean value theorem for integrals for  $f(x)=3{x}^{2}$ on the interval $[-2,2].$
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the mean value theorem for integrals, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c)(b-a) & ={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ f(c) & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2-(-2)}{\int }_{-2}^{2}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{4}\cdot ({x}^{3})|}_{-2}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[{2}^{3}-(-2)^{3}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 16 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the expression for $f(x)$ to solve for the value of $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c) & =4 \\ 3{c}^{2} & =4 \\ {c}^{2} & =\frac{4}{3} \\ c & =\pm \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find all values of $c$ that satisfy the mean value theorem for integrals for  $f(x)=5\sqrt{{x}^{3}}$ on the interval $[0,2].$
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the mean value theorem for integrals, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c)(b-a) & ={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ f(c) & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2-0}{\int }_{0}^{2}5\sqrt{{x}^{3}}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{2}\cdot (2{x}^{5/2})|}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[2\cdot {2}^{5/2}-2\cdot {0}^{5/2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 8\sqrt{2} \\  & =4\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the expression for $f(x)$ to solve for the value of $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c) & =4\sqrt{2} \\ 5\sqrt{{c}^{3}} & =4\sqrt{2} \\ c & =\sqrt[3]{\frac{32}{25}}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the value of $c$ that satisfies the mean value theorem for integrals for $f(x)=4+\frac{2}{{x}^{3}}$ on the interval $[1,2].$
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the mean value theorem for the integrals, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c)(b-a) & ={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ f(c) & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2-1}{\int }_{1}^{2}(4+\frac{2}{{x}^{3}})\text{d}x \\  & ={(4x-\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =(4\cdot 2-\frac{1}{{2}^{2}})-(4\cdot 1-\frac{1}{{1}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{31}{4}-3 \\  & =\frac{19}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the expression for $f(x)$ to solve for the value of $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c) & =\frac{19}{4} \\ 4+\frac{2}{{c}^{3}} & =\frac{19}{4} \\ \frac{2}{{c}^{3}} & =\frac{3}{4} \\ \frac{{c}^{3}}{2} & =\frac{4}{3} \\ {c}^{3} & =\frac{8}{3} \\ c & =\sqrt[3]{\frac{8}{3}} \\ c & =\frac{2}{\sqrt[3]{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Applying the mean value theorem for the integrals. we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c)(b-a) & ={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ f(c) & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2-(-2)}{\int }_{-2}^{2}(-x+2)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{4}\cdot (-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+2x)|}_{-2}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-\frac{{2}^{2}}{2}+2\cdot 2)-(-\frac{(-2)^{2}}{2}+2\cdot (-2))] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[2-(-6)] \\  & =2.\end{aligned}

questions.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x)={x}^{3}-2x$ on the interval $[-2,1].$
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{1-(-2)}{\int }_{-2}^{1}({x}^{3}-2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{-2}^{1}({x}^{3}-2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{3}(\frac{1}{4}{x}^{4}-{x}^{2})|}_{-2}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[(\frac{1}{4}\cdot {1}^{4}-{1}^{2})-(\frac{1}{4}\cdot (-2)^{4}-(-2)^{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(-\frac{3}{4}-0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: A biologist found that the population $P$ of some bacteria in a petri dish can be modeled by the function $P(t)=200+8\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}t),$ where $t$ is the number of hours after $12$ noon. Find the average number of bacteria during the period from $12$ noon to $4$ p.m.
questions.worked_solution:
Since the function is valid starting from $12$ P.M., we can conclude our interval is $[0,4].$

Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}P(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{4-0}{\int }_{0}^{4}(200+8\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}t))\text{d}t \\  & ={\frac{1}{4}(200t-\frac{32}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi \,t}{4}))|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(200\cdot 4-\frac{32}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi \cdot 4}{4}))-(200\cdot 0-\frac{32}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi \cdot 0}{4}))] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(800-\frac{32}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ))-(-\frac{32}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(800-\frac{32}{\pi }\cdot (-1))+\frac{32}{\pi }\cdot 1] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[800+\frac{32}{\pi }+\frac{32}{\pi }] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(800+\frac{64}{\pi }) \\  & =200+\frac{16}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi -0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{cos}^{6}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

We calculate this integral using a substitution $u=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we have 

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,⟹\,\text{d}u=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives

| $x$ | $0$ | $\pi $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $-1$ |

We now substitute and evaluate, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }{cos}^{6}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{1}^{-1}{u}^{6}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-{\frac{1}{\pi }(\frac{{u}^{7}}{7})|}_{1}^{-1} \\  & =-\frac{1}{7\pi }[(-1)^{7}-{1}^{7}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{7\pi }(-2) \\  & =\frac{2}{7\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Within the interval $[-\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}],$ determine the average value of $g(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡3x.$
questions.worked_solution:
Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}g(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\frac{\pi }{2}-(-\frac{\pi }{2})}{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡3x-\operatorname{cos}⁡3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{\pi }(-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡3x-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡3x)|}_{-\pi /2}^{\pi /2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{3\pi }[(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}))-(\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot (-\frac{\pi }{2}))+\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot (-\frac{\pi }{2})))] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3\pi }[(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{2}))-(\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{3\pi }{2})+\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{3\pi }{2}))] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3\pi }[(0+(-1))-(0+1)] \\  & =-\frac{1}{3\pi }(-2) \\  & =\frac{2}{3\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

To solve for $c\ne 0,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{ave}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 0 & =\frac{1}{c-0}{\int }_{0}^{c}(12{x}^{2}-16x-12)\,\text{d}x \\ 0 & ={\frac{1}{c}(4{x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}-12x)|}_{0}^{c} \\ 0 & =\frac{1}{c}[(4{c}^{3}-8{c}^{2}-12c)-0] \\ 0 & =4{c}^{2}-8c-12 \\ 0 & =4({c}^{2}-2c-3) \\ 0 & =4(c-3)(c+1) \\ c & =-1,\,3\end{aligned}

questions.problem: Find $c$ such that the average value of $f(x)=-3\sqrt{x}$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $-6.$
questions.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}\,{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ -6 & =\frac{1}{c-0}\,{\int }_{0}^{c}(-3\sqrt{x})\,\text{d}x \\ -6 & ={\frac{1}{c}(-2{x}^{3/2})|}_{0}^{c} \\ -6 & =\frac{1}{c}[(-2{c}^{3/2})-(0)] \\ -6 & =-2\sqrt{c} \\ \sqrt{c} & =3 \\ c & =9\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081209/assets/7eddb6203ccc3eead9a2a89d7868d3206af52be4c269962e33c551ddd3cf08cd.png)

The graph of the function $f(x),$ which is defined on $[-4,4],$ is shown above. It consists of six line segments.  Find the average value of $f(x)$ on $[-1,3].$
questions.worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval $[a,b]$ is

$$
{f}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the additive property of the definite integral, we write

$$
{\int }_{-1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-1}^{1}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.
$$

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-1,1].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 1 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [1,3].$ The corresponding region is a triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =1+2 \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the formula for the average, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3-(-1)}\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{3}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval $[a,b]$ is

$$
{f}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the additive property of the definite integral, we write

$$
{\int }_{-3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{-3}^{3}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.
$$

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [-3,3].$ The corresponding region is a semi-cirle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot {3}^{2} \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [3,5].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{2}+2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the formula for the average value, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5-(-3)}\cdot (\frac{9\pi }{2}+2) \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{16}+\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}

canonical_examples.problem: Find the values of $c$ that satisfy the mean value theorem for integrals for  $f(x) = x^2-2x+2$ on the interval $[0,3].$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Applying the mean value theorem for integrals, we have

$$
\eqalign{
       f(c) (b-a)  & =  \int_a^b f(x) \, \textrm dx \[5pt]
              f(c)    & = \dfrac {1}{b-a} \int_a^b f(x) \, \textrm dx \[5pt]
    & = \dfrac {1}{3-0} \int_0^3  (x^2-2x+2) \, \textrm dx \[5pt]
     & =  \left . \dfrac {1}{3} \cdot  \left[\dfrac{x^3}{3} -x^2 +2x\right] \right|_0^3 \[5pt]
    & =   \dfrac {1}{3} \cdot \left[ \left(\dfrac{3^3}{3} -3^2 +2\cdot3\right) -  \left(\dfrac{0^3}{3} -0^2 +2\cdot0\right)\right] \[5pt]
    & =  \dfrac {1}{3}\cdot6 \[5pt]
    &  = 2.
}
$$

    

Now, we use the expression for $f(x)$ to solve for the value of $c\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c) & =2 \\ {c}^{2}-2c+2 & =2 \\ c(c-2) & =0 \\ c & =0,2.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Average Value of a Function Over a Given Interval
canonical_examples.problem: Find the average value of the function $f(x) = x - 2$ on the interval $[-2, 4].$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}\,{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{4-(-2)}{\int }_{-2}^{4}x-2\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}-2x){|}_{-2}^{4} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[(\frac{{4}^{2}}{2}-2(4))-(\frac{(-2)^{2}}{2}-2(-2))] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[(8-8)-(2+4)] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(0-6) \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding an Interval Given the Average Value of a Function
canonical_examples.problem: Find $c$ such that the average value of $g(x) = 3 x$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $3.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}\,{\int }_{a}^{b}g(x)\,\text{d}x \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{c-0}\,{\int }_{0}^{c}3x\,\text{d}x \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{c}(\frac{3{x}^{2}}{2}){|}_{0}^{c} \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{c}(\frac{3{c}^{2}}{2}-0) \\ 3 & =\frac{3c}{2} \\ c & =2\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Average Value of a Function Given a Graph
canonical_examples.problem:
The graph of the function $f(x),$ which is defined on $[1,6],$ is shown below. The areas of the regions between the graph and the $x$-axis are $5$ and $2,$ respectively (from left to right). Find the average value of $f(x)$ on $[1,6].$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14081209/assets/6433d1ca57ceb334f304e894e2655ef50d987567fbcf219314302bb381fd9a83.png)
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval is

$$
f_\textrm{avg} = \dfrac{1}{b-a}\int_a^b f(x) \: \textrm{d}x.
$$

Here, we see that

$$
\int_{1}^{6} f(x)\: \textrm{d}x = -5 + 2 = -3.
$$

So, applying the average value formula, we find that the average value is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6-1}\cdot (-3) \\  & =-\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
